doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Preferring small groups to big bands
summary: Jolly says he liked big bands but preferred trios and quintets because the pianist can stretch out.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: When I got out here and I started to work with a trio or a quintet, I liked small group work. Because you could stretch out more as a pianist. In the big band, you get an occasional solo or you’re comping for each tenor player that wants to play ten choruses apiece. You know what I mean.
Yeah, right. That long line of horn players.

And pretty soon it’s always the piano player and the bass player that’s last. And you’ve been doing this for — But I enjoyed big bands, don’t get me wrong. I just preferred the smaller groups, the quintets, the quartets, the trios.
